label: History
value: Anne was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne was orphaned as a sickly infant when both her parents succumbed to fever. At eleven years old, she was mistakenly sent to Prince Edward Island to be adopted by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert of Green Gables, who had originally requested a boy. Despite early mishaps, including broken slates, accidental liniment cake baking, and green dyed hair, Anne won over her adoptive family and the local community of Avonlea. She formed an enduring bond with her best friend Diana Barry and maintained a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe. Anne attended Queen's Academy, winning the Avery Scholarship, but elected to remain at Green Gables to teach locally and care for Marilla. She later earned her B.A. at Redmond College in Kingsport, where she published her writing, made new friends like Philippa Gordon, and eventually reconciled her feelings for Gilbert Blythe. After marrying Gilbert, the couple settled into their 'house of dreams,' where they had a child named Little Jem and Anne formed a close friendship with her neighbor Leslie Moore.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye is taken in by Mrs. George Pye.
unit: Anthony Pye is taken in by his uncle's wife, Mrs. George Pye, and attends the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. Initially, he harbors a strong contempt for Anne, declaring that girl teachers are no good and disrupting the classroom with mischievous acts such as pouring slate bottle water down Aurelia Clay's neck. He continues his defiance by placing a live mouse in Anne's desk drawer, prompting her to whip him with a hardwood pointer. Unexpectedly, this punishment earns his respect, leading him to offer to carry her books and openly admit that she is capable after all. When Anne resigns from her teaching position, Anthony vents his grief by engaging in two pitched battles with other students.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina's daughter married.
unit: After her daughter married and left for the foreign mission field, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. Her relative Stella suggested she move to Kingsport to keep house at Patty's Place for Stella, Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon during their studies at Redmond College. She moved into Patty's Place bringing two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and eventually adopted Rusty as well. She kept house for the girls throughout their remaining college years, providing warm support and practical wisdom. After the students graduated and scattered, she traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field.

She kept house for the girls throughout their remaining college years, providing warm support and practical wisdom. After the students graduated and scattered, she traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field.

label: History
value: Billy grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Billy grew up in Avonlea as part of the Andrews family. As a young man, he admired Anne Shirley immensely and drove her, along with Diana Barry and Jane Andrews, to a concert at the White Sands Hotel, though he decamped before supper out of shyness. He attended local gatherings and spent evenings quietly watching Anne. When his father gave him the upper farm in his own name, he wished to marry Anne but was too shy to propose himself, so he sent his sister Jane to ask her on his behalf. After Anne rejected the proposal, he married Nettie Blewett instead, and they 'appeared out' at the Avonlea church together.

Over fifty years ago, he lost his true love, Margaret, when she drifted out to sea in a storm, a grief he quietly held for the rest of his life. After welcoming Anne and Gilbert Blythe to their home at the Four Winds harbor, he became one of their closest companions and hosted them frequently at his lighthouse. He introduced them to his personal journal, known as his 'life-book', which recorded his many wild and brave adventures at sea. When Owen Ford visited Four Winds, Captain Jim agreed to let him adapt his life-book into a novel, incorporating his memories of Margaret into the storyline. The following autumn, Owen's published novel arrived at the lighthouse, and Captain Jim spent his final evening joyously celebrating its release with Anne and Leslie. Later that night, he passed away peacefully in his sleep, holding his open life-book, and was buried in the over-harbor graveyard.

label: History
value: Charlotta worked as a handmaiden for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge.
unit: At fourteen years old, Charlotta worked as a handmaiden for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. She assisted in entertaining guests such as Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, using a tin horn to trigger the famous echoes across the river. Charlotta took immense care of her mistress and worried deeply whenever Miss Lavendar appeared lonely or unwell. When Stephen Irving returned to reunite with Miss Lavendar, Charlotta helped Anne prepare the house and eagerly supported the romance. Following Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving's wedding, Charlotta moved with them to Boston. She returned to Echo Lodge during summer vacations, where she continued to welcome Anne Shirley with affection. Later, Charlotta married an American named Tom, a bricklayer, but obtained his consent to travel back to Prince Edward Island to attend Anne Shirley's wedding.

Charlotta took immense care of her mistress and worried deeply whenever Miss Lavendar appeared lonely or unwell. When Stephen Irving returned to reunite with Miss Lavendar, Charlotta helped Anne prepare the house and eagerly supported the romance. Following Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving's wedding, Charlotta moved with them to Boston. She returned to Echo Lodge during summer vacations, where she continued to welcome Anne Shirley with affection. Later, Charlotta married an American named Tom, a bricklayer, but obtained his consent to travel back to Prince Edward Island to attend Anne Shirley's wedding.

label: History
value: Miss Cornelia Bryant lives in an emerald house in Four Winds.
unit: Miss Cornelia Bryant lives in an emerald house in Four Winds and is well known throughout the community for her sharp wit, staunch Presbyterianism, and tireless helpfulness. When Anne Blythe moves to Four Winds, Miss Cornelia promptly visits her and recognizes her as a kindred spirit belonging to 'the race that knows Joseph.' She acts as a loyal and devoted friend to Leslie Moore, standing by her through years of hardship. When Gilbert Blythe proposes an operation to cure Dick Moore, Miss Cornelia vehemently opposes the idea out of sympathy for Leslie's plight, though she eventually accepts the outcome when the truth about Dick's identity is revealed. Over the years, she frequently visits Anne and Gilbert, engaging in playful, fiery debates with Captain Jim. Eventually, she astounds her friends by announcing her engagement to Marshall Elliott after he cuts his long-standing beard.

When Anne Blythe moves to Four Winds, Miss Cornelia promptly visits her and recognizes her as a kindred spirit belonging to 'the race that knows Joseph.' She acts as a loyal and devoted friend to Leslie Moore, standing by her through years of hardship. When Gilbert Blythe proposes an operation to cure Dick Moore, Miss Cornelia vehemently opposes the idea out of sympathy for Leslie's plight, though she eventually accepts the outcome when the truth about Dick's identity is revealed. Over the years, she frequently visits Anne and Gilbert, engaging in playful, fiery debates with Captain Jim. Eventually, she astounds her friends by announcing her engagement to Marshall Elliott after he cuts his long-standing beard.

label: History
value: Mary Keith died.
unit: Following the death of his mother Mary Keith, Davy and his twin sister Dora were brought to Green Gables by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley. At first, Davy created endless trouble through constant restlessness, pulling Dora's hair, dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, locking Dora in a duck-house, and telling falsehoods. Under Anne's loving influence and discipline, he developed a deep affection for her and gradually strived to be well-behaved. He attended Avonlea School, where he sat with Milty Boulter and enjoyed playing with other boys. After his uncle Richard Keith passed away, a trust fund was established for Davy and Dora, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. As he grew older, he developed a strong interest in farming and sought to take over running the Green Gables farm.

At first, Davy created endless trouble through constant restlessness, pulling Dora's hair, dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, locking Dora in a duck-house, and telling falsehoods. Under Anne's loving influence and discipline, he developed a deep affection for her and gradually strived to be well-behaved. He attended Avonlea School, where he sat with Milty Boulter and enjoyed playing with other boys. After his uncle Richard Keith passed away, a trust fund was established for Davy and Dora, allowing them to remain permanently at Green Gables. As he grew older, he developed a strong interest in farming and sought to take over running the Green Gables farm.

label: History
value: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope
unit: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope in Avonlea. When Anne Shirley moved to Green Gables, the two met in the Orchard Slope garden and swore eternal friendship over an imagined running stream. They spent their childhood building playhouses such as Idlewild, roaming the woods, rowing on the pond, creating creative writing stories together, and exchanging notes and secrets. After accidentally becoming intoxicated on Marilla Cuthbert's homemade currant wine, she was briefly forbidden by her mother from associating with Anne until Anne saved her little sister Minnie May during an attack of croup. Diana later attended Avonlea School, where her popularity caused her name to frequently appear on the porch walls. She joined the Avonlea Improvement Society as a young adult and eventually married Fred Wright. A few years into her marriage, she gave birth to a daughter whom she named Small Anne Cordelia in honor of her lifelong friendship with Anne.

unit: Diana Barry grew up at Orchard Slope in Avonlea. When Anne Shirley moved to Green Gables, the two met in the Orchard Slope garden and swore eternal friendship over an imagined running stream. They spent their childhood building playhouses such as Idlewild, roaming the woods, rowing on the pond, creating creative writing stories together, and exchanging notes and secrets. After accidentally becoming intoxicated on Marilla Cuthbert's homemade currant wine, she was briefly forbidden by her mother from associating with Anne until Anne saved her little sister Minnie May during an attack of croup. Diana later attended Avonlea School, where her popularity caused her name to frequently appear on the porch walls. She joined the Avonlea Improvement Society as a young adult and eventually married Fred Wright. A few years into her marriage, she gave birth to a daughter whom she named Small Anne Cordelia in honor of her lifelong friendship with Anne.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up at the Glen.
unit: Dick Moore grew up at the Glen, where his father Abner kept a store. He became obsessed with Leslie West and forced her into marrying him by threatening to have his father foreclose the mortgage on her mother's farm. After living with Leslie for one winter on the West farm, he grew tired of quiet married life and left for Nova Scotia. There he joined his cousin George Moore aboard the ship Four Sisters bound for Havana. While in Cuba, Dick contracted yellow fever and died thirteen years prior to the events of Four Winds. His cousin George stayed behind to nurse him, missed the ship's departure, and subsequently suffered an injury that caused loss of memory, leading everyone in Four Winds to mistake George for Dick for twelve years.

label: History
value: Dora's mother died.
unit: Following the death of her sickly mother, six-year-old Dora and her twin brother Davy were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert at Green Gables. Unlike her mischief-making brother, Dora quickly proved to be exceptionally quiet and well-behaved, assisting with household tasks such as picking up chips, wiping dishes, and feeding chickens. She began attending Avonlea school alongside Davy, sitting with her classmates and behaving as a model pupil. When their uncle Richard Keith passed away, he left a fund in trust to secure their permanent home at Green Gables. As she grew older, Dora inherited Anne's former porch room and developed into a sensible, helpful teenager. By the age of seventeen, she began receiving courtships from Ralph Andrews.

Unlike her mischief-making brother, Dora quickly proved to be exceptionally quiet and well-behaved, assisting with household tasks such as picking up chips, wiping dishes, and feeding chickens. She began attending Avonlea school alongside Davy, sitting with her classmates and behaving as a model pupil. When their uncle Richard Keith passed away, he left a fund in trust to secure their permanent home at Green Gables. As she grew older, Dora inherited Anne's former porch room and developed into a sensible, helpful teenager. By the age of seventeen, she began receiving courtships from Ralph Andrews.

label: History
value: Gilbert returned to Avonlea school after summering in New Brunswick.
unit: Upon returning to Avonlea school after summering in New Brunswick, Gilbert playfully teased Anne Shirley by calling her 'Carrots', causing her to smash a slate over his head and refuse to speak to him for years. Despite her persistent hostility, Gilbert maintained a good-natured academic rivalry with Anne, eventually winning the medal at Queen's Academy. Upon graduation, he surrendered his post as teacher of the Avonlea school to Anne so she could stay near Green Gables, finally establishing a warm friendship between them. While teaching at White Sands, he co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Anne before both departed for Redmond College. At Redmond, he excelled academically, served as Freshman class president, and realized his deep love for Anne, though she initially rejected his proposal of marriage. Following his graduation with top honours, Gilbert nearly died of typhoid fever, which brought about a mutual realization of their true feelings. After recovering, he married Anne and relocated to Four Winds Harbor to take over the medical practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Blythe.

unit: Upon returning to Avonlea school after summering in New Brunswick, Gilbert playfully teased Anne Shirley by calling her 'Carrots', causing her to smash a slate over his head and refuse to speak to him for years. Despite her persistent hostility, Gilbert maintained a good-natured academic rivalry with Anne, eventually winning the medal at Queen's Academy. Upon graduation, he surrendered his post as teacher of the Avonlea school to Anne so she could stay near Green Gables, finally establishing a warm friendship between them. While teaching at White Sands, he co-founded the Avonlea Village Improvement Society alongside Anne before both departed for Redmond College. At Redmond, he excelled academically, served as Freshman class president, and realized his deep love for Anne, though she initially rejected his proposal of marriage. Following his graduation with top honours, Gilbert nearly died of typhoid fever, which brought about a mutual realization of their true feelings. After recovering, he married Anne and relocated to Four Winds Harbor to take over the medical practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Blythe.

label: History
value: In early April, Mr. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm adjoining Green Gables in Avonlea.
unit: In early April, Mr. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm adjoining Green Gables in Avonlea, quickly earning a reputation as an eccentric bachelor and a crank. He initially clashed with his neighbor Anne Shirley after his Jersey cow repeatedly broke into her oatfield. After Anne accidentally sold his cow mistaking it for her own, she brought him a cake to apologize, leading to a surprising tea and the beginning of a close friendship between them. value: Jane grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane grew up in Avonlea and attended school with Anne Shirley and their circle of friends. She joined the Queen's class organized by Miss Stacy, successfully passed the Entrance examinations, and attended Queen's Academy, where she excelled in the domestic science course and earned her teaching license. Upon graduating, she accepted a teaching post in Newbridge, where she maintained order strictly and earned a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. She actively participated in local village efforts, such as serving as a committee member for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. After teaching at Newbridge, she was hired to teach at the Avonlea school before accepting a position on the western prairies. During a winter break from Redmond College, she proposed to Anne on behalf of her shy brother Billy, though Anne declined. Later, Jane returned home from the West and married Edward Inglis, a wealthy English millionaire. Following her marriage, she went on a wedding tour to Europe before settling into a prosperous home in Winnipeg, remaining warm and friendly toward her old Avonlea companions.

label: History
value: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea as a member of the Pye family. At school, she was known for cheating on spelling, making fun of Anne Shirley, and challenging her classmates to dares, including a dangerous dare that resulted in Anne falling from a roof and injuring her ankle. She participated in local events, winning first prize for knitted lace at the exhibition and taking part in school dialogues and concerts. When Miss Stacy formed the Queen's class, Josie joined and eventually passed the entrance examinations, barely scraping through. While attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, she remained notoriously sharp-tongued and critical of others. Unlike her classmates who became teachers, Josie chose to return to Queen's for further education. Later, her family home hosted a farewell party given by the Avonlea Improvement Society, and her family's telephone line was known for eavesdropping on neighbors.

unit: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea as a member of the Pye family. At school, she was known for cheating on spelling, making fun of Anne Shirley, and challenging her classmates to dares, including a dangerous dare that resulted in Anne falling from a roof and injuring her ankle. She participated in local events, winning first prize for knitted lace at the exhibition and taking part in school dialogues and concerts. When Miss Stacy formed the Queen's class, Josie joined and eventually passed the entrance examinations, barely scraping through. While attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, she remained notoriously sharp-tongued and critical of others. Unlike her classmates who became teachers, Josie chose to return to Queen's for further education. Later, her family home hosted a farewell party given by the Avonlea Improvement Society, and her family's telephone line was known for eavesdropping on neighbors.

value: Lavendar is a romantic woman.
unit: Lavendar is a romantic, imaginative, and sweet-tempered woman who retains a youthful spirit and dislikes feeling old. She frequently indulges in daydreaming and play-acting, such as inventing imaginary guests for tea or holding conversations with her woods' echoes. While generally warm, sweet, and hospitable, she admits to having a proud and sulky streak when deeply hurt.

label: History
value: Lavendar lived a secluded life.
unit: Lavendar lived a secluded, quiet life at Echo Lodge, a small stone house in Grafton built by her father. Following a youthful quarrel with her fiancé Stephen Irving, the engagement was broken and Stephen moved to the United States. Lavendar remained single in her isolated home, keeping company with her young maidservant, Charlotta the Fourth, and her imaginative 'dream people.' Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon Echo Lodge by accident while trying to find their way to West Grafton and bonded instantly with her. Anne eventually introduced Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to Lavendar, forging a sweet friendship between them. When Stephen returned to Prince Edward Island years later, Anne helped facilitate a meeting between the estranged lovers. Lavendar and Stephen reconciled and were married in the garden of Echo Lodge the following August. Following their wedding, they moved to Boston with Paul and Charlotta the Fourth, returning to spend their summers at Echo Lodge.

label: History
value: Leslie West grew up in Four Winds
unit: Leslie West grew up in Four Winds amidst financial struggles and family tragedies, losing her brother Kenneth and discovering her father after he committed suicide. She excelled academically at Queen's Academy with dreams of attending Redmond College, but sacrificed her ambitions when her mother begged her to marry Dick Moore to save their mortgaged farm. Shortly after their marriage, Dick left on a sea voyage; twelve years later, Captain Jim brought back an amnesiac imbecile believed to be Dick, whom Leslie faithfully nursed in near-poverty for eleven years. Upon meeting Anne Blythe, Leslie gradually let down her defensive barriers and formed a deep, emotional friendship, though she struggled with jealousy over Anne's happy life. When writer Owen Ford stayed as her summer boarder, they fell in love, which plunged Leslie into anguish over her marital trap. Dr. Gilbert Blythe eventually persuaded Leslie to send her husband to Montreal for a trephining operation; the procedure restored his memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's double-cousin, George Moore, and that Dick had died of yellow fever years prior in Cuba. Freed from her burden, Leslie returned home and accepted Owen Ford's proposal of marriage.

unit: Leslie West grew up in Four Winds amidst financial struggles and family tragedies, losing her brother Kenneth and discovering her father after he committed suicide. She excelled academically at Queen's Academy with dreams of attending Redmond College, but sacrificed her ambitions when her mother begged her to marry Dick Moore to save their mortgaged farm. Shortly after their marriage, Dick left on a sea voyage; twelve years later, Captain Jim brought back an amnesiac imbecile believed to be Dick, whom Leslie faithfully nursed in near-poverty for eleven years. Upon meeting Anne Blythe, Leslie gradually let down her defensive barriers and formed a deep, emotional friendship, though she struggled with jealousy over Anne's happy life. When writer Owen Ford stayed as her summer boarder, they fell in love, which plunged Leslie into anguish over her marital trap. Dr. Gilbert Blythe eventually persuaded Leslie to send her husband to Montreal for a trephining operation; the procedure restored his memory, revealing that he was actually Dick's double-cousin, George Moore, and that Dick had died of yellow fever years prior in Cuba. Freed from her burden, Leslie returned home and accepted Owen Ford's proposal of marriage.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with her shy brother Matthew in quiet routine until they decided to adopt an orphan boy to assist with farm duties. Through a mistake, a young girl named Anne Shirley arrived instead; though Marilla initially planned to send her back, she eventually agreed to keep and raise her. Over the years, Marilla disciplined and educated Anne, gradually coming to love her deeply as her own child and softening in temperament. Following Matthew's death, Marilla faced severe headaches and sight problems, considering selling Green Gables until Anne decided to remain home to assist her. Later, Marilla agreed to take in her distant relative's orphaned twin children, Davy and Dora Keith, and hosted Mrs. Rachel Lynde as a co-resident at Green Gables. She lived to see Anne grow up, attend college, marry Gilbert Blythe, and give birth to her children.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott grew up on the over-harbor side of Four Winds.
unit: Marshall Elliott grew up on the over-harbor side of Four Winds as a staunch Liberal. During a heated political campaign fifteen years ago, he vowed publicly not to shave or cut his hair until his political party came into power. He strictly maintained this vow despite his party losing that election and remaining out of power for fifteen years. He spent time fishing with Captain Jim and visiting friends around Four Winds, where he joined Anne, Gilbert, Leslie, and Captain Jim to celebrate New Year's Eve at the lighthouse. When the Liberals finally won the general election, he immediately forced a reluctant local barber to shave his beard and trim his hair past midnight. After fulfilling his vow, he courted and married Cornelia Bryant, moving into her green house to live with her.

label: Personality
value: Matthew is extremely shy.
unit: Extremely shy, quiet, and reserved, Matthew hated going among strangers or speaking in public, and he stood in dread of women and girls with the exception of his sister Marilla and Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Despite his bashfulness, he possessed a gentle, sympathetic nature and a quiet, stubborn persistency when he set his mind on something. He enjoyed talkative companions who did not expect him to converse, and he formed a deep, affectionate bond with Anne Shirley, frequently encouraging and indulging her.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived at Green Gables with his unmarried sister, Marilla. Intending to adopt an orphan boy to assist with farmwork, Matthew drove to Bright River station only to find eleven-year-old Anne Shirley waiting instead. Touched by her chatter and imaginative spirit during the drive home, Matthew quietly insisted to Marilla that they keep her. Over the following years, he became Anne's steadfast supporter, giving her a gift of a fashionable dress with puffed sleeves for Christmas and encouraging her academic pursuits. As he aged, he suffered from severe heart trouble and worked beyond his physical capacity. After learning of the sudden failure of the Abbey Bank where all his savings were deposited, Matthew collapsed and died instantly of the shock. He was buried in the Avonlea graveyard, where Anne continued to visit his grave long after his passing.

label: History
value: Owen Ford recovered from typhoid.
unit: After recovering from typhoid, Owen Ford traveled to Four Winds on his doctor's orders and boarded at the house among the willows with Leslie Moore. He visited Anne Blythe and Captain Jim, who showed him his "life-book." Recognizing its potential, Owen collaborated with Captain Jim during the summer to weave the sea captain's life story and the romance of lost Margaret into a novel. Throughout the summer, he fell deeply in love with Leslie, but believing she was bound to her invalid husband, he kept his feelings secret and left Four Winds distraught after completing his manuscript. After Dick Moore's true identity was discovered and Leslie was freed, Owen returned to Four Winds the following August. He proposed to Leslie in Anne's garden, crowning her hair with a red rose, and she accepted. His novel, titled The Life-Book of Captain Jim, was published to great success in the autumn, and he arranged to purchase the house of dreams to use for summer vacations.

value: > Please, teacher, I found these in Mr. Wright’s field, and I came back to give them to you because I thought you were the kind of lady that would like them, and because . . . I like you, teacher.

label: Quotes
value: > I never got really acquainted with him until after my little mother died. But he’s splendid when you do get to know him. I love him the best in all the world, and Grandma Irving next, and then you, teacher.

label: Quotes
value: > Mrs. Lynde, father made a pretty good job of picking out my first mother and I could trust him to pick out just as good a one the second time.

label: Quotes
value: > I knew I could trust father to pick me out a nice little second mother. It’s a fine thing to have a father you can depend on, teacher.

label: History
value: Paul Irving came from the United States to live with his grandmother in Avonlea after his mother passed away.
unit: After his mother passed away, Paul Irving came from the United States to live with his grandmother in Avonlea, attending the local school under Anne Shirley. He and Anne instantly formed a close bond as kindred spirits, and he became her favorite pupil. During his time at school, he befriended his teacher, introduced her to his rich imaginative world, and occasionally visited Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. When his father, Stephen Irving, came to visit Avonlea, Paul unwittingly helped reunite his father with Miss Lavendar, leading to their marriage. Following the wedding, Paul moved to Boston to live with his father and stepmother, while continuing to visit Echo Lodge in Prince Edward Island during summer vacations. As he grew older, he outgrew his imaginary childhood playmates and turned his attention to sports and writing. His poetry began to be accepted by magazines, earning praise from Anne. At nineteen, he returned to Avonlea to attend Anne's wedding before departing for two years of study abroad.

label: History
value: Philippa meets Anne Shirley
unit: Philippa meets Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in an old graveyard during her early days at Redmond College, instantly taking a liking to them and drawing them into her exclusive social circle. During her first year, she struggles constantly to choose between two home suitors, Alec and Alonzo, while enjoying college life and class rivalry. For their second year, she moves into Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue with Anne, Priscilla, and Stella, helping to set up their household. She falls deeply in love with Jonas (Jo) Blake, a serious minister, and holds firm against her mother's disapproval until her family yields and accepts him. After graduating from Redmond, she marries Jo in Bolingbroke with Anne serving as her bridesmaid. Later, she has children with Jo and visits Anne at Green Gables the day before Anne's wedding to Gilbert Blythe, sending a handmade baby garment to Anne during her time in Four Winds.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school, where he was known for maintaining a poor standard of discipline while devoting his energy primarily to preparing his oldest scholars for Queen's Academy. During his tenure, he openly courted one of his older pupils, Prissy Andrews, frequently helping her with lessons and bestowing gifts on her. In class, he frequently used public discipline, such as forcing Anne Shirley to stand at the blackboard with her name misspelled or compelling her to sit on the boys' side next to Gilbert Blythe. At a local evening concert, he performed Mark Antony's oration over the dead body of Caesar. At the end of June, he delivered an emotional farewell speech to his students upon his departure from Avonlea school, leaving several pupils in tears.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley, forming a close friendship with her and Stella Maynard. After graduating, she taught school at Carmody before returning to teach at her home school. She later attended Redmond College in Kingsport, boarding with Anne Shirley and subsequently moving into Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue with Anne, Philippa Gordon, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina. Upon completing her studies at Redmond, Priscilla married a handsome foreign missionary and moved to Japan with him.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived in Lynde's Hollow on the Avonlea main road, where she kept close watch over everything passing by while running local church societies and knitting quilts. When Matthew Cuthbert brought orphan Anne Shirley to Green Gables, Rachel was astonished and visited to inspect her; her blunt criticism of Anne's freckles and red hair sparked a fiery temper outburst from the girl. After Anne delivered a dramatic apology, Rachel forgave her, allowed her to pick lilies in her garden, and gradually grew to admire her progress and beauty over the years. Following a severe illness with the grippe, Rachel continued her energetic community work, including heading church bazaars, political rallies, and advising Marilla Cuthbert on raising children. When her meek husband Thomas fell ill and passed away, Rachel was forced to sell their mortgaged farm. Rather than move out West with her children or live with her daughter Eliza, she accepted Marilla's invitation to move into Green Gables to live together. She continued supervising household life at Green Gables, helping care for the adopted twins Davy and Dora Keith, and attending church events despite occasional accidents like twisting her ankle or falling down cellar stairs. Years later, she happily helped prepare for Anne's wedding to Gilbert Blythe at Green Gables, bringing homemade gifts and plum pudding to visit Anne and Gilbert in Four Winds for Christmas.

After two years of close companionship and devotion, Roy proposed to Anne in a seaside park pavilion during their graduation season. However, Anne realized she did not truly love him and rejected his proposal, leaving him heartbroken. Roy eventually recovered from the heartache and went on with his life.

label: History
value: Ruby attended Avonlea School
unit: Ruby attended Avonlea School, where she studied alongside Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Jane Andrews. As a student, she joined the Queen's Academy preparation class and later moved to Charlottetown to attend Queen's, where she was recognized as the handsomest girl of her year. After graduating with her teacher's license, she took a teaching position at Carmody, though she returned home to Avonlea on weekends. She had a wide circle of suitors and enjoyed a lively social life. After contracting a severe lung infection during a winter term, she developed galloping consumption, forcing her to give up her teaching plans for the White Sands school. During her final summer, she spent many quiet evenings talking with Anne Shirley in the Gillis garden, expressing her deep fear of death and her longing for a long life with her loved one, Herb Spencer. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter, leaving behind an unfinished piece of embroidery for Anne.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees as Avonlea's first female teacher. Upon taking charge of the school, she introduced various educational innovations, including physical culture exercises, field afternoons in the woods to study nature, and bi-weekly recitation sessions. In November, she organized a Christmas concert with her pupils to raise funds for a schoolhouse flag. Recognizing potential in her advanced students, she organized a specialized class to tutor them after hours for the Queen's Academy entrance examination. Although she considered accepting a job offer in her home district at the end of her first year, she elected to return to Avonlea to see her students through their exams. Following another successful school year, she accompanied her pupils to town for their entrance examinations before finishing her tenure at Avonlea school. Years later, she visited Avonlea and was invited to dinner at Green Gables alongside Mr. and Mrs. Allan.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy.
unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, where she stood out as one of the most attractive and imaginative students. After graduating from Queen's, she spent several years teaching school before deciding to continue her education at Redmond College. Prior to her arrival at Redmond, Stella proposed that she, Anne, Priscilla, and her aunt set up a shared home, leading them to rent Patty's Place. During their time at Patty's Place, Stella managed the household accounts and spent her final college years diligently studying for her degree. After achieving a good all-round standing at graduation, Stella eventually moved to Vancouver to teach.

unit: Stella Maynard attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant, where she stood out as one of the most attractive and imaginative students. After graduating from Queen's, she spent several years teaching school before deciding to continue her education at Redmond College. Prior to her arrival at Redmond, Stella proposed that she, Anne, Priscilla, and her aunt set up a shared home, leading them to rent Patty's Place. During their time at Patty's Place, Stella managed the household accounts and spent her final college years diligently studying for her degree. After achieving a good all-round standing at graduation, Stella eventually moved to Vancouver to teach.

label: Quotes
value: > Now for breakfast. I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.

label: Quotes
value: > You just take it easy, Mrs. Doctor, dear. Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning.

label: Quotes
value: > Is it not funny nobody ever asked me to marry him, Mrs. Doctor, dear? I am no beauty, but I am as good-looking as most of the married women you see. But I never had a beau. What do you suppose is the reason?

label: Quotes
value: > Well, I never could see but that my bread rose just as light when Grits were in as when they were not. And if any party, Mrs. Doctor, dear, will make it rain before the week is out, and save our kitchen garden from entire ruination, that is the party Susan will vote for.

label: Quotes
value: > Well, I never was much hand for weeping, Mrs. Doctor, dear. I would rather fall to and cheer people up than weep with them. Now, do not you cry and spoil your pretty eyes. This house is very well and has served your turn, but it is high time you had a better.

label: Personality
value: Susan is a handmaiden.
unit: Susan is a kind-hearted, industrious, and fiercely loyal handmaiden who takes immense pride in her household duties and cooking. Though grim-faced and prone to dark, resigned proverbs about human trouble, she prefers to cheer people up rather than weep with them. She holds a deep, affectionate devotion toward Anne and her child, often declaring herself to be 'at the helm.' She is fond of men, admits candidly that she enjoys seeing a well-looking man, and holds strong opinions about cellars, pantries, and ears.

label: History
value: Susan Baker was installed as the maid-of-all-work for Gilbert and Anne Blythe.
unit: Susan Baker was installed as the maid-of-all-work for Gilbert and Anne Blythe at their little house of dreams in Four Winds. She grew to worship 'young Mrs. Doctor' with intense fervor and took complete charge of the kitchen and household management. During Anne's dangerous labor and the loss of her first baby, Joy, Susan wept bitterly for her mistress's grief and lovingly cared for her during her recovery. She remained employed at the little house through the birth of Little Jem, guarding the child fiercely and taking charge whenever Anne was away. When her sister Matilda broke her leg, Susan temporarily left to care for her, but returned as soon as possible to resume her duties. When Gilbert bought the Morgan house at the Glen, Susan rejoiced over the larger quarters and superior cellar, ultimately helping the family pack up and move from the little house.
